title: Flat quotient with projective reduction gives split sequence of completions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $u:K\to E$ and $v:E\to M$ be $R$-linear maps such that $u$ is injective, $v$ is surjective, and $\operatorname{im}(u)=\ker(v)$. Assume $M$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $M/IM$ is projective over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For each $R$-module $L$, define $\widehat L=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}L/I^nL$ as the module of compatible residue classes with componentwise operations, where $I^nL$ is generated by $rx$ for $r\in I^n$, $x\in L$. Define $\widehat u:\widehat K\to\widehat E$ and $\widehat v:\widehat E\to\widehat M$ by applying the maps induced by $u$ and $v$ at each quotient level. Then $\widehat u$ is injective, $\widehat v$ is surjective, $\operatorname{im}(\widehat u)=\ker(\widehat v)$, and there is an $R$-linear map $s:\widehat M\to\widehat E$ with $\widehat v\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{\widehat M}$.

proof.text: Put $A_n=R/I^n$ and $L_n=L/I^nL$ for $L=K,E,M$, with reduction maps $q_n^L$. Apply [lem-trf-adic-quotient-projective-short-exact] to the given $u,v$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given short exact sequence, flatness of $M$ and projectivity of $M/IM$. Thus every $0\to K_n\xrightarrow{u_n}E_n\xrightarrow{v_n}M_n\to0$ is exact with $u_n$ injective, $v_n$ surjective and $M_n$ projective over $A_n$, and the displayed reduction squares commute.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, quotient exactness and projectivity of the quotients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-adic-projective-compatible-sections] to the original surjection $v:E\to M$. Step 1 supplies its hypothesis that every $M_n$ is projective over $A_n$. It provides $A_n$-linear sections $s_n:M_n\to E_n$ for all $n\ge1$, with $v_ns_n=\mathrm{id}_{M_n}$ and $q_n^Es_{n+1}=s_nq_n^M$. These are the sections of the very quotient maps of Step 1, since both nodes define $v_n([e])=[v(e)]$.

source.place: Tag 05D3, lemma-split-completed-sequence, induction of compatible sections.

proof.text: For a compatible family $(m_n)\in\widehat M$ define $s((m_n))=(s_n(m_n))$. Step 2 gives $q_n^E(s_{n+1}(m_{n+1}))=s_n(q_n^M(m_{n+1}))=s_n(m_n)$, so this is a compatible family in $\widehat E$. Each $s_n$ is $A_n$-linear, hence $R$-linear; componentwise operations therefore make $s$ $R$-linear. At every level $v_ns_n=\mathrm{id}_{M_n}$, so $\widehat v\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{\widehat M}$ and $\widehat v$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 05D3, passage from compatible quotient splittings to the split completion sequence.

proof.text: If $\widehat u(k)=0$ for $k=(k_n)\in\widehat K$, then $u_n(k_n)=0$ for every $n$; Step 1 gives $k_n=0$ for every $n$, hence $k=0$. Thus $\widehat u$ is injective. If $e=(e_n)\in\ker(\widehat v)$, Step 1 gives a unique $k_n\in K_n$ with $u_n(k_n)=e_n$. Write $a_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$ and $b_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ for reduction. Then $u_n(a_n(k_{n+1}))=b_n(u_{n+1}(k_{n+1}))=b_n(e_{n+1})=e_n=u_n(k_n)$. Injectivity of $u_n$ gives $a_n(k_{n+1})=k_n$. Thus $(k_n)\in\widehat K$ maps to $e$. Conversely $v_nu_n=0$ at every level, so $\widehat v\widehat u=0$. Therefore $\operatorname{im}(\widehat u)=\ker(\widehat v)$. Together with Step 3 this gives every conclusion.
